mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals more weekday circulation and lunch-time foot traffic, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls versus the last 28 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and falls week by week, more trips out of home are converted into discretionary shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC upward within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 15 points while declining for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 15 and continues declining but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates broader outing intensity and neighborhood circulation, which spills over into retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS rise for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following month, reject the interaction.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops sharply below its current trough, access to shopping districts deteriorates immediately and RETAIL_REC will fall within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -75 points or declines by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below the trigger but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days, reject the claim.

mechanism_narrative: A stronger negative gap between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL means more people stay home while commuting remains limited, which suppresses retail errands and lowers RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -30 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 15
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -30 and RESIDENTIAL above 15 yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility in the same week indicates better outdoor weather and more general outing propensity, which should translate into higher retail-and-recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by at least 5 points but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both recover together, routine outside-home activity becomes denser and supports add-on discretionary purchases, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both trend up for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below the prior four-week mean, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening control, a continued decline in TRANSIT combined with weak WORKPLACES mobility signals shrinking urban access, which should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep weakening under tightening restrictions but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, reject the mechanism.
